anthropic.humanValidation: Clio framework validation in publisher paper; no per-user occupation verification
anthropic.interpretation: Observed platform task-use context and global interaction modes, not exposure, national adoption or occupational automation
limitations: December 2024/January 2025 Free/Pro Claude.ai sample
Nonrepresentative platform population; not US-only
Task-text ambiguity and legacy taxonomy splits are retained
Published interaction shares total 84.209%; no renormalization or headline reconstruction
Data README explicitly permits CC-BY but does not specify version; MIT card refers to code
anthropic.measurementLevel: task usage and global interaction categories
anthropic.publication: Which Economic Tasks are Performed with AI? Evidence from Millions of Claude Conversations
anthropic.sourceTaxonomy: Historical O*NET-SOC 2010 code membership verified; exact task database version not supplied

felten.authorsInstitution: Edward Felten, Manav Raj, Robert Seamans
felten.interpretation: General AI application/ability overlap, not exclusively LLM exposure
limitations: Deferred: repository has no explicit data license; article CC-BY not assumed to license separately hosted files
Historical capabilities differ from GenAI task rubric
felten.publication: Occupational, industry, and geographic exposure to artificial intelligence: A novel dataset and its potential uses
felten.sourceTaxonomy: SOC study vintage; explicit mapping required

gpts_are_gpts.authorsInstitution: Tyna Eloundou, Sam Manning, Pamela Mishkin, Daniel Rock
gpts_are_gpts.interpretation: Potential same-quality task time savings under explicit LLM/software rubric; not a displacement probability
limitations: Static early-LLM capability vintage
Subjective human/model classifications
Adoption, demand expansion and job loss not identified
Core weight is 2; not time share or current task importance
Multiple O*NET children remain separate canonical records
gpts_are_gpts.publication: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
gpts_are_gpts.sourceTaxonomy: O*NET-SOC 2019; authors task snapshot 27.1 and rating references 27.2

ilo.authorsInstitution: Pawel Gmyrek et al. / ILO and NASK
ilo.interpretation: Task automation potential/exposure gradients; not observed job loss
limitations: Not integrated: no accepted score download plus verified licensed SOC mapping
Many-to-many ISCO/SOC relations require independent review
ilo.publication: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure

imf.interpretation: Exposure and complementarity are separate methodological concepts
limitations: Not integrated: no independently cleared pinned occupational data artifact
AIPI country preparedness is not occupational exposure
imf.publication: Gen-AI: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work

microsoft.authorsInstitution: Kiran Tomlinson, Sonia Jaffe, Will Wang, Scott Counts, Siddharth Suri
microsoft.humanValidation: Published validation; platform classification remains model-mediated
microsoft.interpretation: Platform-derived applicability from user-goal and AI-action completion/scope, source IWA weighting; not national adoption or automation
limitations: US Bing Copilot sample January–September 2024
Selected users/activities, not representative workers
Seven broad aggregates and five unmapped reporting hybrids retained
Native percentile population mixes reporting levels
Nonphysical AI-side definition pinned to v1.1; cannot silently compare prior versions
microsoft.publication: Working with AI: Measuring the Applicability of Generative AI to Occupations
microsoft.sourceTaxonomy: Publisher SOC 2018 with mixed OEWS reporting aggregates; accepted exact detailed/broad matches only

nber_task_framework.authorsInstitution: Erik Brynjolfsson, Tom Mitchell, Daniel Rock
nber_task_framework.interpretation: Historical task-based general machine-learning suitability, not current LLM usage
limitations: Reviewed conceptual benchmark; no additional licensed pinned numeric table accepted
Do not treat historical machine-learning suitability as current GenAI capability
nber_task_framework.publication: What Can Machines Learn, and What Does It Mean for Occupations and the Economy?

stanford.authorsInstitution: Erik Brynjolfsson, Bharat Chandar, Ruyu Chen / Stanford Digital Economy Lab
stanford.humanValidation: Study-specific controls; not independent exposure validation
stanford.interpretation: Empirical employment comparator, not a new distributable task backbone
limitations: Deferred: underlying ADP panel not licensed for redistribution
Public dashboard viewing does not establish raw-data permissions
Uses academic exposure constructs already reviewed here
